# Canon: naturalloy

How naturalloy says an Alloy formula in English, and why. It is the canon of the package `@bigmistqke/naturalloy`. It writes its terms and claims in Alloy. naturalloy itself says its statements from them, through the [Alloy plugin](../canon-plugin-alloy/README.md) of the canon checker.

<!-- toc:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
- [`@term verbalizer`](#term-verbalizer) — The verbalizer is the part of naturalloy that says a formula in words, from a table of readings that says each name of the formula.
- [`@term formula`](#term-formula) — A formula is a piece of Alloy that states a claim, and that the verbalizer says in words.
- [`@term quantified-formula`](#term-quantified-formula) — A quantified formula is a formula that declares variables, and the verbalizer names them and says their types.
- [`@term quantifier`](#term-quantifier) — A quantifier is a formula that declares a variable and says something of it, which the verbalizer may say as a noun phrase.
- [`@term fit`](#term-fit) —
  > A [quantifier](#term-quantifier) fits a noun phrase exactly when all of these hold:
  > - the reading of the quantifier does not say the variable twice
  > - the quantifier has a fact for its variable beside another thing
  > - the quantifier does not both say that no variable differs from another and hold a condition
  > - the condition of the quantifier is about its variable
  > - the quantifier does not have several conditions, one of which begins with a time phrase
- [`@term predicate-call`](#term-predicate-call) — A predicate call is a formula that names a predicate and gives its arguments.
- [`@term definition-passage`](#term-definition-passage) — A definition is a predicate with a body that the verbalizer says as what its name means exactly when the body holds.
- [`@term by-kind`](#term-by-kind) —
  > A [definition](#term-definition-passage) can be said kind by kind exactly when the definition has none of these:
  > - an alternative that does not begin with its kind
  > - a run of "and" beside another alternative of its kind
  > - an alternative that says something about another unit
  > - two kinds that can share a member
- [`@term linked-formula`](#term-linked-formula) — A linked formula is a formula that has a word whose reading a unit holds, and the statement may link that word.
- [`@term series`](#term-series) — A series is a run of clauses, or a rule of two sides. The verbalizer says it as a sentence, as bullets or on one line.
- [`@term sentenceable`](#term-sentenceable) —
  > A [list](#term-series) can be put in a sentence exactly when all of these hold:
  > - the list has three clauses or fewer
  > - the list has only items that are one clause
  > - at least one of these holds:
  >   - the list has no item that holds a comma
  >   - the list has two clauses or fewer
  > - the list fits a line when it is put in a sentence
  > - the list has no clause before its last that begins with a time phrase
  > - the list has no clause before its last with a relative clause in it
- [`@term line`](#term-line) — A line is one line of a table of readings, which gives a word of the logic its sentences.
- [`@term pass`](#term-pass) — A pass is one named change to how the verbalizer says a statement. A pass of the IR changes the sentence a formula was lowered to. A pass of the printer changes the words the printer lays it out in.
- [`@term pipeline`](#term-pipeline) — The pipeline is the passes in the order they run: each sees the IR the one before it left.
- [`@fact every-moment-has-a-next-moment`](#fact-every-moment-has-a-next-moment) — In Alloy 6, a trace is infinite: every moment has exactly one next moment.
- [`@fact the-analyzer-wraps-integers-at-their-bit-width`](#fact-the-analyzer-wraps-integers-at-their-bit-width) — With its default options, the analyzer keeps every integer in a fixed bit width. A number that leaves that range wraps around into it.
- [`@fact the-analyzer-divides-toward-zero-and-gives-the-sign-for-zero`](#fact-the-analyzer-divides-toward-zero-and-gives-the-sign-for-zero) — The analyzer rounds `div[a, b]` toward zero, and gives -1, 0 or 1 for `div[a, 0]` as `a` is positive, zero or negative. `rem[a, b]` has the sign of `a`, and `rem[a, 0]` is `a`.
- [`@fact the-analyzer-shifts-by-the-lowest-bits-of-the-amount`](#fact-the-analyzer-shifts-by-the-lowest-bits-of-the-amount) — The analyzer shifts by the number in the lowest bits of the amount: as many bits as it takes to count to the bit width.
- [`@axiom a-formula-is-said-without-loss`](#axiom-a-formula-is-said-without-loss) — The verbalizer says a formula only in words that translate it without loss, and refuses a formula that it cannot say that way.
  - [`@spec a-statement-is-said-through-passes-that-each-keep-its-meaning`](#spec-a-statement-is-said-through-passes-that-each-keep-its-meaning) — The verbalizer lowers a formula to the IR in the plainest words its readings give. It makes each choice of words in a [pass](#term-pass) of the [pipeline](#term-pipeline). A pass of the IR changes no meaning. The analyzer asks that of every change it makes to the sweep.
    - [`@spec every-pass-changes-the-words-of-a-formula-of-the-sweep`](#spec-every-pass-changes-the-words-of-a-formula-of-the-sweep) — Every [pass](#term-pass) changes the words of at least one formula of the sweep.
    - [`@spec a-pass-runs-after-the-passes-whose-shapes-it-reads`](#spec-a-pass-runs-after-the-passes-whose-shapes-it-reads) — Where one pass makes or removes a shape that another reads, the [pipeline](#term-pipeline) runs them in the order the shape needs.
      - [`@spec a-negation-moves-inward-before-noun-phrases-are-said`](#spec-a-negation-moves-inward-before-noun-phrases-are-said) — For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2: when pass_1 moves a negation inward and pass_2 says a quantifier as a noun phrase, pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec two-things-of-a-kind-are-paired-before-noun-phrases-are-said`](#spec-two-things-of-a-kind-are-paired-before-noun-phrases-are-said) — For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2: when pass_1 says two things of a kind as one and another and pass_2 says a quantifier as a noun phrase, pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec noun-phrases-are-said-before-there-is-a-that`](#spec-noun-phrases-are-said-before-there-is-a-that) —
        > For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2:
        >
        > when all of these hold:
        > - pass_1 says a quantifier as a noun phrase
        > - pass_2 says a quantifier of its variable alone as "there is a … that"
        >
        > then pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-before-quantifiers-of-for-every-become-one`](#spec-a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-before-quantifiers-of-for-every-become-one) —
        > For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2:
        >
        > when all of these hold:
        > - pass_1 says a set equal to a variable as that variable and no other
        > - pass_2 makes nested quantifiers of "for every" one
        >
        > then pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec until-is-said-in-a-sentence-before-a-time-phrase-goes-in-front`](#spec-until-is-said-in-a-sentence-before-a-time-phrase-goes-in-front) —
        > For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2:
        >
        > when all of these hold:
        > - pass_1 says until and since of two clauses as one sentence
        > - pass_2 puts a time phrase in front of the words it covers
        >
        > then pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec a-time-phrase-goes-in-front-before-clauses-become-a-sentence`](#spec-a-time-phrase-goes-in-front-before-clauses-become-a-sentence) — For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2: when pass_1 puts a time phrase in front of the words it covers and pass_2 says a few clauses as one sentence, pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec clauses-become-a-sentence-before-a-rule-goes-on-one-line`](#spec-clauses-become-a-sentence-before-a-rule-goes-on-one-line) — For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2: when pass_1 says a few clauses as one sentence and pass_2 says a rule on one line, pass_1 runs before pass_2.
      - [`@spec clauses-become-a-sentence-before-their-shared-words-are-said-once`](#spec-clauses-become-a-sentence-before-their-shared-words-are-said-once) —
        > For every [pass_1](#term-pass) and every pass_2:
        >
        > when all of these hold:
        > - pass_1 says a few clauses as one sentence
        > - pass_2 says the subject and the verb that negative clauses share once, before "none of these"
        >
        > then pass_1 runs before pass_2.
    - [`@spec a-pass-weighs-only-words-that-no-later-pass-changes`](#spec-a-pass-weighs-only-words-that-no-later-pass-changes) — The words a [pass](#term-pass) weighs to choose how to say a part are the words that part ends with: no pass after it changes them.
      - [`@bug a-time-phrase-weighs-a-part-that-a-later-pass-changes`](#bug-a-time-phrase-weighs-a-part-that-a-later-pass-changes) — The verbalizer weighs whether a time phrase goes in front before it lays out the rule or the list the phrase covers. So a time phrase can stay above a rule that ends on one line.
  - [`@spec a-formula-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-formula-is-said-in-full) — The verbalizer says every part of a [formula](#term-formula), and leaves none unsaid.
  - [`@spec a-formula-is-said-the-same-way-every-time`](#spec-a-formula-is-said-the-same-way-every-time) — The verbalizer says a formula in the same words every time.
  - [`@spec saying-a-formula-ends`](#spec-saying-a-formula-ends) — The verbalizer ends on every formula, with words or with a refusal.
  - [`@spec a-refusal-is-told-apart-from-a-fault`](#spec-a-refusal-is-told-apart-from-a-fault) — The verbalizer refuses a formula only with a `Refusal`, and anything else it throws is a fault of the verbalizer.
  - [`@spec a-rewrite-means-what-the-formula-it-replaces-means`](#spec-a-rewrite-means-what-the-formula-it-replaces-means) — Where the verbalizer says a formula through another, the two hold at the same moments, for every value of their free variables.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-is-said-with-the-noun-of-its-type-for-each-variable`](#spec-a-quantifier-is-said-with-the-noun-of-its-type-for-each-variable) — The verbalizer says each variable of a [quantified formula](#term-quantified-formula) once, with the noun of its type.
  - [`@spec three-things-a-for-every-names-are-a-list`](#spec-three-things-a-for-every-names-are-a-list) — When "for every" or "for some" names three things or more, the verbalizer lists them: "for every cleanup, every owner_1 and every owner_2".
  - [`@spec some-of-several-things-is-said-as-for-some`](#spec-some-of-several-things-is-said-as-for-some) — The verbalizer says `some` over several variables as "for some" each of them, followed by what holds of them, the way it says `all` as "for every".
  - [`@spec a-for-every-right-inside-a-for-every-is-one-for-every`](#spec-a-for-every-right-inside-a-for-every-is-one-for-every) — The verbalizer says a "for every" whose formula is another "for every" as one, with the variables of both: "for every cleanup and every owner".
  - [`@spec a-variable-is-named-after-its-noun-and-its-number`](#spec-a-variable-is-named-after-its-noun-and-its-number) — Where a variable needs a number, the verbalizer names it after its noun and its number among the variables of that noun.
  - [`@spec a-variable-alone-of-its-noun-is-named-the-noun`](#spec-a-variable-alone-of-its-noun-is-named-the-noun) — The verbalizer names a variable "the" and its noun, with no number, when a quantifier says it first. No other variable may have its noun, and no other word of the statement may say that noun.
  - [`@spec a-for-every-over-the-noun-alone-is-said-as-a-noun-where-the-words-first-name-it`](#spec-a-for-every-over-the-noun-alone-is-said-as-a-noun-where-the-words-first-name-it) — Take a "for every" over one variable that is named the noun alone. The words may first name the variable in the first side of a rule, or as the subject of a definition. There, the verbalizer leaves the "for every" out. It says that first name as "a" or "an" and the noun, and each later one as "the" and the noun. The words must name the variable again after the first time.
    - [`@spec a-rule-over-every-thing-of-a-kind-says-a-noun-in-its-when`](#spec-a-rule-over-every-thing-of-a-kind-says-a-noun-in-its-when) — The verbalizer says a "for every" over one variable as the rule it holds, where that rule has no "otherwise". Its first side says "a" and the noun: "when a cleanup has run, code has registered the cleanup".
    - [`@spec a-definition-of-every-thing-of-a-kind-says-a-noun-as-its-subject`](#spec-a-definition-of-every-thing-of-a-kind-says-a-noun-as-its-subject) — The verbalizer says a definition over one parameter as its words alone, where they open with the parameter. Their subject is "a" and the noun: "a unit is unfounded exactly when the unit is one of these".
    - [`@spec a-variable-named-once-keeps-its-for-every`](#spec-a-variable-named-once-keeps-its-for-every) — Where the words name the variable of a "for every" only once, the verbalizer keeps the "for every".
    - [`@spec a-rule-with-an-otherwise-keeps-its-for-every`](#spec-a-rule-with-an-otherwise-keeps-its-for-every) — The verbalizer keeps the "for every" of a rule that has an "otherwise".
  - [`@spec a-variable-is-named-the-same-however-the-formula-names-it`](#spec-a-variable-is-named-the-same-however-the-formula-names-it) — The verbalizer names the variables the same way, whatever names the formula gives them.
  - [`@spec some-is-said-with-an-article-chosen-by-the-sound-of-the-noun`](#spec-some-is-said-with-an-article-chosen-by-the-sound-of-the-noun) — The verbalizer says `some` of a type with the article "a" or "an" that fits the sound of the noun.
  - [`@spec an-article-the-noun-is-written-with-wins-over-its-sound`](#spec-an-article-the-noun-is-written-with-wins-over-its-sound) — When the noun of a type carries an article, the verbalizer uses that article, whatever the sound of the noun.
  - [`@spec no-over-several-variables-is-said-as-no-combination`](#spec-no-over-several-variables-is-said-as-no-combination) — The verbalizer says `no` over variables of several types as no combination of the variables.
  - [`@spec one-as-a-quantifier-is-said-as-exactly-one`](#spec-one-as-a-quantifier-is-said-as-exactly-one) — The verbalizer says `one` over a variable as "exactly one" of its noun, and over several variables as exactly one combination of them.
  - [`@spec lone-as-a-quantifier-is-said-as-at-most-one`](#spec-lone-as-a-quantifier-is-said-as-at-most-one) — The verbalizer says `lone` over a variable as "at most one" of its noun, and over several variables as at most one combination of them.
  - [`@spec a-block-as-the-body-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-its-formulas-together`](#spec-a-block-as-the-body-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-its-formulas-together) — The verbalizer says a quantifier whose body is a block, `all x: T { a b }`, as the quantifier with the formulas of the block holding together.
  - [`@spec a-call-of-a-predicate-gives-its-variables-numbers-that-are-free`](#spec-a-call-of-a-predicate-gives-its-variables-numbers-that-are-free) — When a called body quantifies a variable that the call already uses, the verbalizer gives it a number that no variable in use has.
  - [`@spec a-variable-of-a-body-never-takes-the-name-of-an-argument`](#spec-a-variable-of-a-body-never-takes-the-name-of-an-argument) — The verbalizer never gives a variable of a called body the name of an argument of the call.
  - [`@spec the-alternatives-of-a-list-reuse-a-name-and-keep-it-taken-for-what-follows`](#spec-the-alternatives-of-a-list-reuse-a-name-and-keep-it-taken-for-what-follows) — The verbalizer gives the same name to the variable in each alternative of a list, and keeps the name taken for what follows.
  - [`@spec the-statements-of-a-list-each-use-the-same-names`](#spec-the-statements-of-a-list-each-use-the-same-names) — The verbalizer uses the same names in each statement of a list that quantifies a variable of one type.
  - [`@spec conditions-that-hold-together-keep-their-names-apart`](#spec-conditions-that-hold-together-keep-their-names-apart) — The verbalizer gives a different name to the variable of each condition in a list of conditions that hold together.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body`](#spec-a-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body) — The verbalizer says a [call](#term-predicate-call) of a predicate with no reading by its body, with each argument in the place it fills.
  - [`@spec a-negated-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-as-untrue`](#spec-a-negated-predicate-with-no-reading-is-said-as-untrue) — The verbalizer says a negated call of a predicate with no reading as "it is not the case that", followed by the body. It sets a body that is more than one plain clause apart below those words.
  - [`@spec the-reading-of-the-table-wins-over-the-body`](#spec-the-reading-of-the-table-wins-over-the-body) — The verbalizer says a call of a predicate that has both a reading and a body with the reading.
  - [`@spec the-checker-reads-the-predicates-a-vocabulary-declares`](#spec-the-checker-reads-the-predicates-a-vocabulary-declares) — The verbalizer reads each predicate that a vocabulary declares: its name, what it takes and its body.
  - [`@spec a-call-written-as-a-join-is-said-as-the-call`](#spec-a-call-written-as-a-join-is-said-as-the-call) — The verbalizer says `x.p` and `x.p[y]`, for a predicate `p`, as `p[x]` and `p[x, y]`.
  - [`@spec a-box-join-of-a-field-is-said-as-the-navigation`](#spec-a-box-join-of-a-field-is-said-as-the-navigation) — The verbalizer says `f[x]`, for a field `f`, as `x.f`.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-an-expression-is-said-by-the-body-with-the-expression-in-place`](#spec-a-call-with-an-expression-is-said-by-the-body-with-the-expression-in-place) — The verbalizer says a call of a predicate with no reading by its body also when an argument is an expression. The expression takes the place of the parameter.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-one-value-is-said-through-a-member-in-the-place-of-the-argument`](#spec-a-call-with-one-value-is-said-through-a-member-in-the-place-of-the-argument) — The verbalizer says a call of a predicate with a reading and an argument of one value through a member of its type. That member is the one in the argument.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-an-argument-of-none-or-several-values-is-refused`](#spec-a-call-with-an-argument-of-none-or-several-values-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate with a reading, with an argument that can hold none or several values, and names the argument.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-an-argument-of-another-type-is-refused`](#spec-a-call-with-an-argument-of-another-type-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call whose argument is of a type that shares no member with the type of its parameter, and names both types.
  - [`@spec a-let-is-said-with-its-value-in-the-place-of-its-name`](#spec-a-let-is-said-with-its-value-in-the-place-of-its-name) — The verbalizer says `let x = e | f` as `f` with `e` in the place of `x`. A `let` of several names puts each value in place, in order.
  - [`@spec a-let-whose-value-a-quantifier-of-its-body-would-capture-is-refused`](#spec-a-let-whose-value-a-quantifier-of-its-body-would-capture-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a `let` whose body declares a variable with a name that its value uses, and names the variable.
  - [`@spec a-negation-is-said-with-the-negative-reading-of-what-it-negates`](#spec-a-negation-is-said-with-the-negative-reading-of-what-it-negates) — The verbalizer says the negation of a comparison or a call with the negative reading of what it negates.
  - [`@spec not-before-a-compound-is-said-with-the-not-moved-inward`](#spec-not-before-a-compound-is-said-with-the-not-moved-inward) — The verbalizer says `not` before a list, a rule, an equivalence, a quantifier or a temporal operator as the formula it equals with the `not` moved inward. Where no such formula exists, it says "it is not the case that" before the formula, set apart.
    - [`@spec not-before-an-and-is-said-as-at-least-one-negation`](#spec-not-before-an-and-is-said-as-at-least-one-negation) — The verbalizer says `not (a and b)` as `not a or not b`.
    - [`@spec not-before-an-or-is-said-as-every-negation`](#spec-not-before-an-or-is-said-as-every-negation) — The verbalizer says `not (a or b)` as `not a and not b`.
    - [`@spec not-before-a-rule-is-said-as-its-condition-and-the-negation-of-its-consequence`](#spec-not-before-a-rule-is-said-as-its-condition-and-the-negation-of-its-consequence) — The verbalizer says `not (a implies b)` as `a and not b`.
    - [`@spec not-before-an-equivalence-is-said-as-exactly-one-of-its-sides`](#spec-not-before-an-equivalence-is-said-as-exactly-one-of-its-sides) — The verbalizer says `not (a iff b)` as exactly one of `a` and `b` holding.
    - [`@spec not-before-an-else-is-said-as-the-rule-with-each-side-negated`](#spec-not-before-an-else-is-said-as-the-rule-with-each-side-negated) — The verbalizer says `not (c implies a else b)` as `c implies not a else not b`.
    - [`@spec not-before-some-or-no-is-said-as-the-other`](#spec-not-before-some-or-no-is-said-as-the-other) — The verbalizer says `not some x: T | f` as `no x: T | f`, and `not no x: T | f` as `some x: T | f`.
    - [`@spec not-before-all-is-said-as-some-with-the-body-negated`](#spec-not-before-all-is-said-as-some-with-the-body-negated) — The verbalizer says `not all x: T | f` as `some x: T | not f`.
    - [`@spec not-before-always-or-eventually-is-said-as-the-other-with-the-formula-negated`](#spec-not-before-always-or-eventually-is-said-as-the-other-with-the-formula-negated) — The verbalizer says `not always f` as `eventually not f`, and `not eventually f` as `always not f`.
    - [`@spec not-before-historically-or-once-is-said-as-the-other-with-the-formula-negated`](#spec-not-before-historically-or-once-is-said-as-the-other-with-the-formula-negated) — The verbalizer says `not historically f` as `once not f`, and `not once f` as `historically not f`.
    - [`@spec not-before-after-is-said-as-after-with-the-formula-negated`](#spec-not-before-after-is-said-as-after-with-the-formula-negated) — The verbalizer says `not after f` as `after not f`.
    - [`@spec a-not-with-no-formula-to-move-into-is-said-as-it-is-not-the-case-that`](#spec-a-not-with-no-formula-to-move-into-is-said-as-it-is-not-the-case-that) — The verbalizer says `not` before `one`, `lone`, `before` or a binary temporal operator as "it is not the case that", with the formula it negates set apart below it.
  - [`@spec a-union-on-the-left-is-spelled-out`](#spec-a-union-on-the-left-is-spelled-out) — The verbalizer says a comparison with a union on its left as one statement for each member of the union. For `in` each statement holds, and for `not in` at least one fails.
  - [`@spec a-difference-on-the-right-is-spelled-out`](#spec-a-difference-on-the-right-is-spelled-out) — The verbalizer says a comparison with a difference on its right as: the left side is in the first part and not in the second.
  - [`@spec a-disj-quantifier-is-said-with-its-variables-different`](#spec-a-disj-quantifier-is-said-with-its-variables-different) — The verbalizer says a quantifier with `disj` as the same quantifier with the condition that its variables are different.
  - [`@spec a-difference-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition`](#spec-a-difference-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition) — The verbalizer says a quantifier over `A - B` as a quantifier over `A`, with the condition that the variable is not in `B`. When `B` is a variable, the condition is that the two are different.
  - [`@spec a-set-with-no-noun-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition`](#spec-a-set-with-no-noun-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition) — The verbalizer says a quantifier over a set `S` with no noun over the signature that holds `S`, with the condition that the variable is in `S`.
  - [`@spec an-expression-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition`](#spec-an-expression-as-the-type-of-a-quantifier-is-said-as-a-condition) — The verbalizer says a quantifier over an expression `e`, such as `all o: c.on | …`, as one over the type of `e`, with the condition that the variable is in `e`.
  - [`@spec a-disj-after-the-colon-is-said-as-a-disj-before-the-names`](#spec-a-disj-after-the-colon-is-said-as-a-disj-before-the-names) — The verbalizer says `x, y: disj T` as it says `disj x, y: T`.
  - [`@spec one-before-the-type-of-a-variable-is-said-as-the-type`](#spec-one-before-the-type-of-a-variable-is-said-as-the-type) — The verbalizer says `x: one T`, of a quantifier or of a parameter, as `x: T`.
  - [`@spec a-variable-that-can-hold-several-things-or-none-is-refused`](#spec-a-variable-that-can-hold-several-things-or-none-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a variable declared `lone`, `some` or `set`, or with an arrow in its type, and says that it can hold none or several things.
  - [`@spec private-before-a-variable-of-a-quantifier-is-refused`](#spec-private-before-a-variable-of-a-quantifier-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `private` before a variable of a quantifier, which Alloy does not read.
  - [`@spec membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field`](#spec-membership-in-a-navigation-is-said-with-the-reading-of-its-field) — The verbalizer says `x in y.f` and `y in f.x` with the reading of the field `f`, with `y` in its first slot and `x` in its second.
  - [`@spec no-or-some-of-a-navigation-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-the-type-of-the-field`](#spec-no-or-some-of-a-navigation-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-the-type-of-the-field) — The verbalizer says `no y.f` and `some y.f` as `no` or `some` of the type that the field `f` points at. The reading of the field puts that noun beside `y`.
  - [`@spec a-transpose-in-a-navigation-is-said-as-the-navigation-the-other-way`](#spec-a-transpose-in-a-navigation-is-said-as-the-navigation-the-other-way) — The verbalizer says `y.~f` as `f.y`, and `~f.y` as `y.f`.
  - [`@spec a-pair-in-a-transpose-is-said-the-other-way-round`](#spec-a-pair-in-a-transpose-is-said-the-other-way-round) — The verbalizer says `x->y in ~r` as `y->x in r`.
  - [`@spec some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature`](#spec-some-or-no-of-a-set-of-things-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-of-its-signature) — The verbalizer says `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, as `some` or `no` of the signature that holds `S`. That signature is the one `S` is declared `in` or `extends`, or `S` itself when it stands on its own.
    - [`@spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-once-is-said-with-a-noun-phrase-in-its-place`](#spec-a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-once-is-said-with-a-noun-phrase-in-its-place) — When the reading of `S` says its variable once, the verbalizer puts a noun phrase of the signature in its place: "an edge is being delivered".
    - [`@spec a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-twice-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-set-whose-reading-says-its-variable-twice-is-said-in-full) — When the reading of `S` says its variable more than once, the verbalizer says `some S` and `no S` in full: a quantifier over the signature, with a numbered name.
    - [`@spec a-set-with-no-one-signature-that-holds-it-is-refused`](#spec-a-set-with-no-one-signature-that-holds-it-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `some S` and `no S`, for a set `S` whose reading takes a variable, when the vocabulary declares no one signature that holds `S`, and names `S`.
  - [`@spec a-primed-name-with-no-reading-of-its-own-is-said-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-primed-name-with-no-reading-of-its-own-is-said-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says a clause that primes one set or field as "at the next moment" and the clause without the prime. A reading of the primed name wins.
  - [`@spec two-sets-compared-are-said-member-by-member`](#spec-two-sets-compared-are-said-member-by-member) — The verbalizer says two sets or two relations compared with `in`, `=` or `!=` member by member, over the types of their columns.
  - [`@spec a-field-of-pairs-has-the-types-of-its-columns`](#spec-a-field-of-pairs-has-the-types-of-its-columns) — The verbalizer takes the types of the columns of a field declared with an arrow from its declaration, as `older: Cleanup -> Cleanup` of `Clock`.
  - [`@spec membership-in-an-else-of-sets-is-said-through-each-branch`](#spec-membership-in-an-else-of-sets-is-said-through-each-branch) — The verbalizer says `x in (c implies a else b)` as a rule with an "otherwise": when `c`, `x` is in `a`, and otherwise `x` is in `b`.
  - [`@spec an-integer-in-a-number-is-said-as-equal-to-it`](#spec-an-integer-in-a-number-is-said-as-equal-to-it) — The verbalizer says `y in n`, for a variable `y` that a quantifier declares an integer and a number `n`, as `y = n`.
  - [`@spec all-or-some-over-a-union-of-signatures-is-said-over-each`](#spec-all-or-some-over-a-union-of-signatures-is-said-over-each) — The verbalizer says `all`, `some` or `no` of one variable over a union of signatures that no one type holds as the same quantifier over each signature.
  - [`@spec sides-that-alloy-does-not-compare-are-refused`](#spec-sides-that-alloy-does-not-compare-are-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a comparison of sides that hold tuples of different sizes, or things of types that share no member.
  - [`@spec an-equality-with-a-side-of-unknown-type-is-refused`](#spec-an-equality-with-a-side-of-unknown-type-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `=` or `!=` between two sets when the vocabulary does not tell the type of a side that is not a variable.
  - [`@spec a-field-of-one-value-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-with-its-reading`](#spec-a-field-of-one-value-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-with-its-reading) — The verbalizer says `x.f = y` and `x.f != y`, for a field `f` that the vocabulary declares `one` or `lone`, with the reading of the field.
  - [`@spec a-field-of-many-values-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-member-by-member`](#spec-a-field-of-many-values-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-member-by-member) — Take a field `f` that can hold more than one value, where its reading with `y` is more than one plain clause. The verbalizer says `x.f = y` member by member. For every member of the type of `f`, it says the reading of `f` "exactly when" the member and `y` are the same. It says `x.f != y` as the negation of that.
  - [`@spec a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-as-the-variable-and-no-other`](#spec-a-set-equal-to-a-variable-is-said-as-the-variable-and-no-other) — Take a variable `x`, and a set or a field of many values `s`, where being in `s` is one plain clause. The verbalizer says `s = x` as `x` in `s` "and" no other member of its type in `s`: "the cleanup is on owner_1 and is on no other owner". The second half drops a subject the two share.
  - [`@spec two-values-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member`](#spec-two-values-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member) — The verbalizer says `y.f = z.g` as "for every" member of the type of `f`, the reading of `f` "exactly when" the reading of `g`. When one side is primed, it says that side "at the next moment" and the other "now". It says `y.f != z.g` as the negation of that.
  - [`@spec an-expression-is-said-through-the-types-of-its-columns`](#spec-an-expression-is-said-through-the-types-of-its-columns) — The verbalizer says a formula about an expression through members of the types of its columns. This holds for an expression that is more than a set or a navigation of a variable.
    - [`@spec a-union-on-the-right-is-said-as-or`](#spec-a-union-on-the-right-is-said-as-or) — The verbalizer says `x in a + b`, for a variable or a pair `x`, as `x in a` or `x in b`.
    - [`@spec an-intersection-on-the-right-is-said-as-and`](#spec-an-intersection-on-the-right-is-said-as-and) — The verbalizer says `x in a & b`, for a variable or a pair `x`, as `x in a` and `x in b`.
    - [`@spec not-in-before-a-difference-is-said-as-the-negation-of-in`](#spec-not-in-before-a-difference-is-said-as-the-negation-of-in) — The verbalizer says `x not in a - b` as the negation of `x in a - b`: `x not in a` or `x in b`.
    - [`@spec membership-in-a-navigation-of-an-expression-is-said-as-a-pair-in-it`](#spec-membership-in-a-navigation-of-an-expression-is-said-as-a-pair-in-it) — The verbalizer says `x in y.e`, for a variable `y`, as `y->x in e`, and `x in e.y` as `x->y in e`.
    - [`@spec a-pair-in-a-product-is-said-as-each-side-in-its-part`](#spec-a-pair-in-a-product-is-said-as-each-side-in-its-part) — The verbalizer says `x->y in a -> b` as `x in a` and `y in b`.
    - [`@spec membership-in-a-chain-of-navigations-is-said-through-a-member-between`](#spec-membership-in-a-chain-of-navigations-is-said-through-a-member-between) — The verbalizer says `x in e.f`, where `e` is not one variable, as `some m: T | m in e and x in m.f`. `T` is the type of the last column of `e`.
    - [`@spec membership-in-a-navigation-from-a-signature-is-said-through-a-member-of-it`](#spec-membership-in-a-navigation-from-a-signature-is-said-through-a-member-of-it) — The verbalizer says `x in S.f`, for a signature `S` where `S.f` has no reading of its own, as `some m: S | m->x in f`: "a cleanup is on x".
    - [`@spec membership-in-a-signature-with-no-reading-is-said-with-its-noun`](#spec-membership-in-a-signature-with-no-reading-is-said-with-its-noun) — The verbalizer says `x in S`, for a signature `S` with a noun and no reading, as `x` "is" the noun with its article: "c is a cleanup".
    - [`@spec a-primed-expression-is-said-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-primed-expression-is-said-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `x in e'`, for an expression `e`, as "at the next moment" before `x in e`.
    - [`@spec an-expression-of-a-variable-on-the-left-is-said-member-by-member`](#spec-an-expression-of-a-variable-on-the-left-is-said-member-by-member) — The verbalizer says `e in s`, for an expression `e` that names a variable, as: for every member `m` of the type of `e`, when `m in e`, `m in s`.
    - [`@spec two-expressions-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member`](#spec-two-expressions-that-are-equal-are-said-member-by-member) — The verbalizer says `a = b`, for sides that the specs above do not say, as: for every member `m` of their type, `m in a` exactly when `m in b`. It says `a != b` as the negation of that.
    - [`@spec some-or-no-of-an-expression-is-said-over-the-types-of-its-columns`](#spec-some-or-no-of-an-expression-is-said-over-the-types-of-its-columns) — The verbalizer says `some e` and `no e`, for an expression the specs above do not say, as `some` or `no` over its column types, with the members in `e`.
    - [`@spec one-or-lone-of-an-expression-is-said-as-exactly-or-at-most-one`](#spec-one-or-lone-of-an-expression-is-said-as-exactly-or-at-most-one) — The verbalizer says `one e` and `lone e` as exactly one or at most one member of the types of the columns of `e` in `e`.
    - [`@spec an-expression-whose-types-the-vocabulary-does-not-tell-is-refused`](#spec-an-expression-whose-types-the-vocabulary-does-not-tell-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula about an expression whose column types the vocabulary does not tell, and names the expression.
  - [`@spec an-override-is-said-as-the-pairs-of-its-right-and-the-rest-of-its-left`](#spec-an-override-is-said-as-the-pairs-of-its-right-and-the-rest-of-its-left) — The verbalizer says `x->y in r ++ s` as `x->y in s`, or `x->y in r` and `no x.s`. For sets, `x in a ++ b` is `x in a + b`.
  - [`@spec a-domain-restriction-is-said-as-the-first-member-in-the-set`](#spec-a-domain-restriction-is-said-as-the-first-member-in-the-set) — The verbalizer says `x->y in a <: r` as `x in a` and `x->y in r`.
  - [`@spec a-range-restriction-is-said-as-the-last-member-in-the-set`](#spec-a-range-restriction-is-said-as-the-last-member-in-the-set) — The verbalizer says `x->y in r :> b` as `x->y in r` and `y in b`.
  - [`@spec an-arrow-with-a-multiplicity-is-refused`](#spec-an-arrow-with-a-multiplicity-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses an arrow with a multiplicity, such as `a one -> lone b`, and says that it says how many each side relates.
  - [`@spec a-closure-is-said-as-reaching-in-one-or-more-steps`](#spec-a-closure-is-said-as-reaching-in-one-or-more-steps) — The verbalizer says `x->y in ^r` as `x` "reaches" `y` "in one or more steps", and says what a step is with the reading of `r`.
  - [`@spec a-reflexive-closure-is-said-as-reaching-in-zero-or-more-steps`](#spec-a-reflexive-closure-is-said-as-reaching-in-zero-or-more-steps) — The verbalizer says `x->y in *r` as `x` "reaches" `y` "in zero or more steps", and says what a step is with the reading of `r`.
  - [`@spec some-or-no-of-a-reflexive-closure-is-refused`](#spec-some-or-no-of-a-reflexive-closure-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `some`, `no`, `one` or `lone` of a reflexive closure, and says that it holds every member of every type.
  - [`@spec none-is-said-as-nothing`](#spec-none-is-said-as-nothing) — The verbalizer says `e = none`, `none = e` and `e in none` as `no e`, and `e != none` as `some e`. It leaves `none` out of a union or a difference, and says `x in none` alone as never holding. It takes `none in e`, and a quantifier over `none` but `some` and `one`, as always holding, and says `#none` as 0.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-over-a-variable-is-said-of-the-variable`](#spec-a-quantifier-over-a-variable-is-said-of-the-variable) — The verbalizer says `all x: p | f` and `some x: p | f`, for a variable `p`, as `f` with `p` in the place of `x`, and `no x: p | f` as its negation.
  - [`@spec a-value-in-its-own-builtin-type-always-holds`](#spec-a-value-in-its-own-builtin-type-always-holds) — The verbalizer takes a string in `String`, and an integer variable in `Int`, as a formula that always holds.
  - [`@spec a-formula-that-never-holds-is-refused`](#spec-a-formula-that-never-holds-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that never holds, such as `some none`, and says that it claims what cannot be.
  - [`@spec a-formula-that-never-holds-is-left-out-of-an-or`](#spec-a-formula-that-never-holds-is-left-out-of-an-or) — The verbalizer leaves a formula that never holds, such as `x in none`, out of an `or`.
  - [`@spec a-pair-in-iden-is-said-as-the-same`](#spec-a-pair-in-iden-is-said-as-the-same) — The verbalizer says `x->y in iden` as `x` and `y` being the same.
  - [`@spec univ-is-said-as-a-signature-of-its-own`](#spec-univ-is-said-as-a-signature-of-its-own) — The verbalizer says `univ` as a signature that holds every atom, with the noun the readings give it.
  - [`@spec a-set-comprehension-is-said-through-its-variables`](#spec-a-set-comprehension-is-said-through-its-variables) — The verbalizer says `x in { y: T | f }` as `x in T` and `f` with `x` in the place of `y`, and `{ y: T }` as `T`.
  - [`@spec disj-of-expressions-is-said-as-no-two-sharing-a-member`](#spec-disj-of-expressions-is-said-as-no-two-sharing-a-member) — The verbalizer says `disj[a, b]` as `a` and `b` being different when both are variables, and as `no a & b` otherwise. Over more arguments, it says it of each pair.
  - [`@spec a-string-is-said-as-itself-in-quotes`](#spec-a-string-is-said-as-itself-in-quotes) — The verbalizer says a string in the place of a variable as itself, in quotes: "c is named "abc"".
  - [`@spec an-expression-is-one-thing-where-its-declarations-make-it-so`](#spec-an-expression-is-one-thing-where-its-declarations-make-it-so) — The verbalizer takes an expression for one thing only where the declarations make it so. That covers a variable, a string and a number. It also covers a navigation of a `one` field from one thing, and such an expression primed.
  - [`@spec a-variable-a-quantifier-declares-has-the-type-it-declares`](#spec-a-variable-a-quantifier-declares-has-the-type-it-declares) — In the types of the columns of an expression, the verbalizer takes a variable to be of the type its quantifier declares.
  - [`@spec a-variable-on-the-right-of-in-is-said-as-equal-to-what-is-in-it`](#spec-a-variable-on-the-right-of-in-is-said-as-equal-to-what-is-in-it) — The verbalizer says `x in p`, for a variable `p` that a quantifier declares, as `x = p` where `x` is one thing. Where `x` can hold several things, it says that each of them is `p`.
  - [`@spec some-or-no-of-a-signature-is-said-over-its-members`](#spec-some-or-no-of-a-signature-is-said-over-its-members) — The verbalizer says `some S`, `no S`, `one S` and `lone S` of a signature `S` with a noun and no reading by its noun alone, as `there is an owner`.
  - [`@spec a-count-of-one-thing-is-a-formula-that-always-or-never-holds`](#spec-a-count-of-one-thing-is-a-formula-that-always-or-never-holds) — The verbalizer takes `some`, `one` and `lone` of one thing as a formula that always holds, and `no` of one thing as one that never does.
  - [`@spec a-value-in-a-string-is-said-as-equal-to-it`](#spec-a-value-in-a-string-is-said-as-equal-to-it) — The verbalizer says `x in "a"`, where `x` is [one thing](#spec-an-expression-is-one-thing-where-its-declarations-make-it-so), as `x = "a"`: "c and "a" are the same". It says `x not in "a"` as `x != "a"`.
  - [`@spec set-or-seq-before-an-expression-is-refused`](#spec-set-or-seq-before-an-expression-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `set e` and `seq e` as a formula, and says that Alloy reads them only in a declaration.
  - [`@spec a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line`](#spec-a-rule-of-two-clauses-is-said-on-one-line) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [list](#term-series) is a rule whose two sides are each one clause
    > - the list is not a rule whose first side begins with a time phrase
    >
    > then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list on one line, as "when" the first side, the second side.
  - [`@spec an-equivalence-of-two-clauses-is-said-with-exactly-when`](#spec-an-equivalence-of-two-clauses-is-said-with-exactly-when) — The verbalizer says `a iff b`, when each side is one clause, as `a` "exactly when" `b`.
  - [`@spec an-equivalence-of-more-than-clauses-is-said-as-both-or-neither`](#spec-an-equivalence-of-more-than-clauses-is-said-as-both-or-neither) — The verbalizer says `a iff b`, when a side is more than one clause, as a list of the two sides under "both or neither of these hold".
  - [`@spec an-equivalence-that-is-a-side-of-a-rule-is-said-as-both-or-neither`](#spec-an-equivalence-that-is-a-side-of-a-rule-is-said-as-both-or-neither) — As a side of a rule, of a binary temporal operator or of a definition, the verbalizer says `a iff b` as both or neither.
  - [`@spec an-equivalence-whose-first-side-begins-with-a-time-phrase-is-said-as-both-or-neither`](#spec-an-equivalence-whose-first-side-begins-with-a-time-phrase-is-said-as-both-or-neither) — The verbalizer says `a iff b` as both or neither of its sides when `a` begins with a time phrase. A clause at the next moment and a clause now are the exception.
  - [`@spec a-clause-at-the-next-moment-equal-to-a-clause-now-is-said-with-exactly-when`](#spec-a-clause-at-the-next-moment-equal-to-a-clause-now-is-said-with-exactly-when) — The verbalizer says `a' iff b`, for clauses with no other time phrase, comma, "and", "or" or relative clause, as `a` "at the next moment exactly when" `b` "now".
  - [`@spec an-equivalence-whose-first-side-holds-a-noun-phrase-is-said-as-both-or-neither`](#spec-an-equivalence-whose-first-side-holds-a-noun-phrase-is-said-as-both-or-neither) — The verbalizer says `a iff b` as both or neither of its sides when `a` holds a noun phrase, such as "no owner".
  - [`@spec an-else-is-said-as-otherwise`](#spec-an-else-is-said-as-otherwise) — The verbalizer says `c implies a else b` as the rule "when" `c`, `a`, with "otherwise" before `b`.
  - [`@spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-only-where-it-starts-with-its-own-words`](#spec-a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-only-where-it-starts-with-its-own-words) — A statement begins with a capital where it begins with its own words, and with the name unchanged where it begins with a name.
  - [`@spec two-variables-are-said-to-be-different-or-the-same`](#spec-two-variables-are-said-to-be-different-or-the-same) — The verbalizer says a comparison of two variables as "different" or "the same".
  - [`@spec eventually-is-said-as-now-or-later`](#spec-eventually-is-said-as-now-or-later) — The verbalizer says `eventually` as "now or later".
  - [`@spec after-is-said-as-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-after-is-said-as-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `after` as "at the next moment".
  - [`@spec always-is-said-as-from-now-on`](#spec-always-is-said-as-from-now-on) — The verbalizer says `always` as "from now on", unless what it covers is a rule.
  - [`@spec a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever`](#spec-a-rule-at-every-later-moment-is-said-from-now-on-whenever) — The verbalizer says `always` over a rule as "from now on, whenever" the rule's condition, followed by its consequence.
  - [`@spec before-is-said-as-there-is-a-moment-just-before-and-at-it`](#spec-before-is-said-as-there-is-a-moment-just-before-and-at-it) — The verbalizer says `before` as `there is a moment just before, and at it`.
  - [`@spec once-is-said-as-now-or-earlier`](#spec-once-is-said-as-now-or-earlier) — The verbalizer says `once` as "now or earlier".
  - [`@spec historically-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-earlier-moment`](#spec-historically-is-said-as-now-and-at-every-earlier-moment) — The verbalizer says `historically` as "now and at every earlier moment".
  - [`@spec a-sequence-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-sequence-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `a ; b` as "a, and at the next moment, b".
  - [`@spec a-time-phrase-before-words-that-hold-a-time-phrase-sets-them-apart`](#spec-a-time-phrase-before-words-that-hold-a-time-phrase-sets-them-apart) — Before words with a time phrase of their own, the verbalizer ends a time phrase with a colon and sets the words apart below it.
  - [`@spec an-and-or-an-or-below-a-time-phrase-is-a-list`](#spec-an-and-or-an-or-below-a-time-phrase-is-a-list) — The verbalizer says an "and" or an "or" that a time phrase covers as a list below it, and never as one sentence after it.
  - [`@spec the-spellings-of-not-in-and-not-equal-are-said-alike`](#spec-the-spellings-of-not-in-and-not-equal-are-said-alike) — The verbalizer says `!in`, `! in`, `not =` and `! =` as it says `not in` and `!=`.
  - [`@spec text-that-alloy-does-not-read-is-refused`](#spec-text-that-alloy-does-not-read-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that Alloy does not read, such as `a == b`, with the reason the parser gives.
  - [`@spec a-binary-temporal-operator-is-said-with-its-sides-set-apart`](#spec-a-binary-temporal-operator-is-said-with-its-sides-set-apart) — The verbalizer sets each side of `until`, `since`, `releases` and `triggered` apart when either side is more than one plain clause, and each side of `;` that is. It puts them below the words that place them in time.
    - [`@spec until-is-said-as-two-parts`](#spec-until-is-said-as-two-parts) — When a side is more than one plain clause, the verbalizer says `a until b` in two parts. First comes `b` "now or later", then `a` "at every moment from now until the first such moment, not including it".
    - [`@spec since-is-said-as-two-parts`](#spec-since-is-said-as-two-parts) — When a side is more than one plain clause, the verbalizer says `a since b` in two parts. First comes `b` "now or earlier", then `a` "at every moment after the last such moment, up to and including now".
    - [`@spec until-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence`](#spec-until-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence) — The verbalizer says `a until b` of two plain clauses as one sentence: `b` "now or later, and until then," `a`.
    - [`@spec since-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence`](#spec-since-of-two-plain-clauses-is-one-sentence) — Of two plain clauses, the verbalizer says `a since b` as one sentence. It says `b` "now or earlier", then `a` "at every moment after the last such moment, up to and including now".
    - [`@spec releases-is-said-as-always-or-until`](#spec-releases-is-said-as-always-or-until) — The verbalizer says `a releases b` as `always b or (b until (a and b))`.
    - [`@spec triggered-is-said-as-historically-or-since`](#spec-triggered-is-said-as-historically-or-since) — The verbalizer says `a triggered b` as `historically b or (b since (a and b))`.
    - [`@spec a-sequence-with-a-side-of-more-than-a-clause-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment`](#spec-a-sequence-with-a-side-of-more-than-a-clause-is-said-as-and-at-the-next-moment) — The verbalizer says `a ; b`, with a side that is more than one plain clause, as `a and after b`.
    - [`@spec a-side-with-a-time-phrase-a-noun-phrase-or-a-where-is-more-than-a-plain-clause`](#spec-a-side-with-a-time-phrase-a-noun-phrase-or-a-where-is-more-than-a-plain-clause) — A side is one plain clause only when the verbalizer says it by one reading with a variable in each of its places. It holds no time phrase, no comma, no noun phrase, no relative clause, no "where" and no "it is not the case that".
  - [`@spec this-outside-a-definition-of-a-signature-is-refused`](#spec-this-outside-a-definition-of-a-signature-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `this` outside a predicate or a function of a signature, which Alloy does not read.
  - [`@spec steps-in-a-formula-is-refused`](#spec-steps-in-a-formula-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `steps` in a formula, and says that Alloy reads it only in a scope.
  - [`@spec a-name-of-this-module-is-said-as-the-name`](#spec-a-name-of-this-module-is-said-as-the-name) — The verbalizer says `this/Ran` and `@Ran` as it says `Ran`.
  - [`@spec a-name-of-another-module-is-said-by-its-own-reading`](#spec-a-name-of-another-module-is-said-by-its-own-reading) — The verbalizer says a name of another module, such as `m/Ran`, by the reading of that whole name.
  - [`@spec a-comment-in-a-formula-is-left-out`](#spec-a-comment-in-a-formula-is-left-out) — The verbalizer leaves out a comment in a formula: `--`, `//`, `/* … */` and `/** … */`.
  - [`@spec a-typographic-prime-is-said-as-a-prime`](#spec-a-typographic-prime-is-said-as-a-prime) — The verbalizer says `‘` and `’` as it says `'`.
  - [`@spec an-integer-comparison-is-said-in-integers-that-wrap`](#spec-an-integer-comparison-is-said-in-integers-that-wrap) — The verbalizer says `<`, `>`, `=<`, `>=` and their negations, and `=` and `!=` between two numbers, after "in integers that wrap around at the analyzer's bit width".
    - [`@spec two-numbers-are-compared-with-the-words-of-their-operator`](#spec-two-numbers-are-compared-with-the-words-of-their-operator) — The verbalizer says `<` as "is less than", `>` as "is greater than", `=<` as "is at most", `>=` as "is at least" and `=` as "is equal to". It says a negation with "not".
    - [`@spec a-count-is-said-as-the-number-of-values`](#spec-a-count-is-said-as-the-number-of-values) — The verbalizer says `#e` as "the number of values of" a member of the type of `e`, "such that" the member is in `e`.
    - [`@spec a-sum-over-a-variable-is-said-as-the-sum-over-every-value`](#spec-a-sum-over-a-variable-is-said-as-the-sum-over-every-value) — The verbalizer says `sum x: T | e` as "the sum, over every" member of `T`, "of" `e`.
    - [`@spec a-set-of-integers-where-a-number-belongs-is-said-as-the-sum-of-its-members`](#spec-a-set-of-integers-where-a-number-belongs-is-said-as-the-sum-of-its-members) — The verbalizer says a set of integers where a number belongs, as in `c.n < 3` or `int[c.n]`, as `"the sum of the values of"` an integer in it.
    - [`@spec plus-minus-and-mul-are-said-as-plus-minus-and-times`](#spec-plus-minus-and-mul-are-said-as-plus-minus-and-times) — The verbalizer says `plus[a, b]`, `minus[a, b]` and `mul[a, b]` as `a` "plus", "minus" or "times" `b`.
    - [`@spec a-division-is-said-with-its-rounding-and-its-rule-for-zero`](#spec-a-division-is-said-with-its-rounding-and-its-rule-for-zero) — The verbalizer says `div[a, b]` as `a` "divided by" `b`, rounded toward zero, with its value when `b` is zero. It says `rem[a, b]` as `"the remainder of"` `a` divided by `b`, with its sign and its value when `b` is zero.
    - [`@spec a-number-is-said-as-itself`](#spec-a-number-is-said-as-itself) — The verbalizer says a number in decimal, whether the formula writes it in decimal, in hexadecimal or in binary.
    - [`@spec min-and-max-are-said-as-the-least-and-the-greatest-integer`](#spec-min-and-max-are-said-as-the-least-and-the-greatest-integer) — The verbalizer says `min` and `max` as "the least integer" and "the greatest integer".
    - [`@spec the-spellings-fun-min-fun-max-and-fun-next-are-said-as-min-max-and-next`](#spec-the-spellings-fun-min-fun-max-and-fun-next-are-said-as-min-max-and-next) — The verbalizer says `fun/min`, `fun/max` and `fun/next` as it says `min`, `max` and `next`.
    - [`@spec a-part-of-an-integer-comparison-that-is-more-than-a-number-is-named-below-it`](#spec-a-part-of-an-integer-comparison-that-is-more-than-a-number-is-named-below-it) — The verbalizer names a count, a sum or a division in an integer comparison as `number_1`, `number_2` and so on, and says after "where" what each is.
    - [`@spec a-shift-is-refused`](#spec-a-shift-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `<<`, `>>` and `>>>`, and says that the analyzer shifts by the lowest bits of the amount.
    - [`@spec a-set-compared-with-a-number-is-refused`](#spec-a-set-compared-with-a-number-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `=` and `!=` between a set and a number, such as `c.n = 2`, and names them.
    - [`@spec a-number-outside-an-integer-comparison-is-refused`](#spec-a-number-outside-an-integer-comparison-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a number or a count outside an integer comparison, and names it.
  - [`@spec the-next-integer-is-said-as-the-integer-after`](#spec-the-next-integer-is-said-as-the-integer-after) — The verbalizer says `x->y in next` as `y` "is the integer after" `x` "without wrapping around".
  - [`@spec int-and-seq-int-have-nouns-of-their-own`](#spec-int-and-seq-int-have-nouns-of-their-own) — The verbalizer says `Int` with the noun "integer", and `seq/Int` with the noun "sequence index", unless the readings give another.
  - [`@spec a-name-with-no-reading-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-name-with-no-reading-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula with a name that has no reading, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-reading-with-no-negative-form-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-reading-with-no-negative-form-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that negates a word whose reading has no negative form, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-type-with-no-noun-is-refused-and-named`](#spec-a-type-with-no-noun-is-refused-and-named) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that quantifies a type with no noun, and names the type.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-uses-a-slot-the-formula-does-not-give-is-refused`](#spec-a-reading-that-uses-a-slot-the-formula-does-not-give-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word uses a place that the formula does not fill, and names the place.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-leaves-out-a-slot-the-formula-gives-is-refused`](#spec-a-reading-that-leaves-out-a-slot-the-formula-gives-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula whose reading of a word leaves out a place that the formula fills, and names the place.
  - [`@spec a-binary-temporal-operator-inside-a-side-of-another-is-refused`](#spec-a-binary-temporal-operator-inside-a-side-of-another-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses `until`, `since`, `releases`, `triggered` or `;` with a side that holds one of them, except a `;` after a `;`.
  - [`@spec a-primed-relation-of-a-variable-signature-is-refused`](#spec-a-primed-relation-of-a-variable-signature-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a prime on a relation `Sig.rel` that has a reading of its own when `Sig` is a `var sig`.
  - [`@spec a-construct-the-words-do-not-cover-is-refused`](#spec-a-construct-the-words-do-not-cover-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula with a construct that the words do not cover, and names the construct.
  - [`@spec a-line-of-readings-that-cannot-be-read-is-refused`](#spec-a-line-of-readings-that-cannot-be-read-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a [line](#term-line) of readings that has neither a noun nor a key, and says that it cannot read the line.
  - [`@spec a-bracket-with-no-partner-is-refused`](#spec-a-bracket-with-no-partner-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a line of readings with a bracket that has no partner, and says so.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-whose-body-cannot-be-said-is-refused-with-advice-to-give-it-a-reading`](#spec-a-predicate-whose-body-cannot-be-said-is-refused-with-advice-to-give-it-a-reading) — The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate with no reading and a body the words do not cover, and advises a reading.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-defined-in-terms-of-itself-is-refused`](#spec-a-predicate-defined-in-terms-of-itself-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call of a predicate whose body calls that predicate, and says that it calls itself.
  - [`@spec a-call-with-the-wrong-number-of-arguments-is-refused`](#spec-a-call-with-the-wrong-number-of-arguments-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a call with the wrong number of arguments, and says how many the predicate takes.
  - [`@spec text-that-is-not-a-definition-is-refused`](#spec-text-that-is-not-a-definition-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses text given as a definition that is not one, and says how to write a definition.
  - [`@spec a-parameter-with-no-type-is-refused`](#spec-a-parameter-with-no-type-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition with a parameter that has no type, and says so.
  - [`@spec a-definition-whose-body-is-a-rule-is-said-with-the-rule-set-apart`](#spec-a-definition-whose-body-is-a-rule-is-said-with-the-rule-set-apart) — The verbalizer says a definition whose body is a rule or a "for every" as what it names "exactly when the following holds". It sets the body apart below.
  - [`@spec a-definition-of-a-word-with-no-reading-is-refused`](#spec-a-definition-of-a-word-with-no-reading-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition of a word that has no reading, and names the word.
  - [`@spec a-passage-that-starts-with-pred-is-a-definition`](#spec-a-passage-that-starts-with-pred-is-a-definition) — The verbalizer reads text that starts with the keyword `pred` as a definition.
  - [`@spec a-passage-that-starts-with-fun-is-a-definition`](#spec-a-passage-that-starts-with-fun-is-a-definition) — The verbalizer reads text that starts with the keyword `fun` as a definition.
  - [`@spec private-before-a-definition-changes-nothing-that-is-said`](#spec-private-before-a-definition-changes-nothing-that-is-said) — The verbalizer says a `private pred` or a `private fun` as it says the same definition without `private`.
  - [`@spec parameters-in-round-brackets-are-read-as-in-square-ones`](#spec-parameters-in-round-brackets-are-read-as-in-square-ones) — The verbalizer reads `pred p(x: T)` as `pred p[x: T]`.
  - [`@spec a-comma-before-or-after-the-parameters-is-read-as-none`](#spec-a-comma-before-or-after-the-parameters-is-read-as-none) — The verbalizer reads `pred p[, x: T]` and `pred p[x: T,]` as `pred p[x: T]`.
  - [`@spec a-predicate-of-a-signature-takes-this-as-its-first-parameter`](#spec-a-predicate-of-a-signature-takes-this-as-its-first-parameter) — The verbalizer reads `pred T.p[x: U] { … }` as `pred p[this: T, x: U] { … }`, for its definition and for a call of it.
  - [`@spec a-body-of-several-formulas-is-said-as-them-holding-together`](#spec-a-body-of-several-formulas-is-said-as-them-holding-together) — The verbalizer says a block of formulas on lines of their own, as a body or as a formula, as the formulas holding together.
  - [`@spec an-empty-body-is-said-as-what-the-definition-names`](#spec-an-empty-body-is-said-as-what-the-definition-names) — The verbalizer says a definition with an empty body as what it names, for every parameter.
  - [`@spec a-formula-that-always-holds-is-left-out-of-an-and`](#spec-a-formula-that-always-holds-is-left-out-of-an-and) — The verbalizer leaves a formula that always holds out of an `and`. An empty block is one, and so is a call of a predicate with an empty body.
  - [`@spec a-formula-that-only-always-holds-is-refused`](#spec-a-formula-that-only-always-holds-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a formula that always holds and is not part of an `and`, and says that it claims nothing.
  - [`@spec a-parameter-that-can-hold-several-things-or-none-is-refused`](#spec-a-parameter-that-can-hold-several-things-or-none-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a definition with a parameter declared with `lone`, `some` or `set`, or with an arrow, and names the parameter.
  - [`@spec a-function-is-said-as-its-value-holding-a-member-exactly-when-its-body-does`](#spec-a-function-is-said-as-its-value-holding-a-member-exactly-when-its-body-does) — The verbalizer says `fun f[x: T]: U { e }` as: for every `x` and every member `u` of `U`, the reading of `f` of `x` and `u` "exactly when" `u in e`.
  - [`@spec a-call-of-a-function-with-a-reading-is-said-with-its-reading`](#spec-a-call-of-a-function-with-a-reading-is-said-with-its-reading) — The verbalizer says `y in f[x]`, for a function `f` with a reading, with the reading of `f`, with `x` and then `y` in its slots.
  - [`@spec a-call-of-a-function-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body`](#spec-a-call-of-a-function-with-no-reading-is-said-by-its-body) — The verbalizer says a call of a function with no reading by its body, with each argument in the place of its parameter.
  - [`@spec a-call-of-a-macro-is-said-by-its-body`](#spec-a-call-of-a-macro-is-said-by-its-body) — The verbalizer says a call of a macro, `let m[x] = …` or `let m[x] { … }`, by its body with each argument in the place of its parameter.
  - [`@spec a-macro-as-a-definition-is-refused`](#spec-a-macro-as-a-definition-is-refused) — The verbalizer refuses a macro given as a definition, and says that a parameter of a macro has no type.
  - [`@spec a-definition-says-what-it-names-exactly-when-its-body-holds-for-every-parameter`](#spec-a-definition-says-what-it-names-exactly-when-its-body-holds-for-every-parameter) — The verbalizer says a [definition](#term-definition-passage) as "for every" parameter, then the name, "exactly when", and the body.
  - [`@spec a-definition-that-marks-its-variables-disj-is-said-with-them-different`](#spec-a-definition-that-marks-its-variables-disj-is-said-with-them-different) — The verbalizer says a definition that marks its variables `disj` with the condition that they are different. A call of it said by its body gets the same condition.
  - [`@spec a-definition-with-a-body-of-one-clause-is-said-on-one-line`](#spec-a-definition-with-a-body-of-one-clause-is-said-on-one-line) — The verbalizer says a definition whose body is one clause on one line after the "for every".
  - [`@spec a-definition-whose-body-is-a-series-sets-it-apart`](#spec-a-definition-whose-body-is-a-series-sets-it-apart) — The verbalizer sets apart the body of a [definition](#term-definition-passage) that is a series, below "exactly when the following holds".
  - [`@spec a-definition-says-each-parameter-with-the-noun-of-its-type`](#spec-a-definition-says-each-parameter-with-the-noun-of-its-type) — The verbalizer says each parameter of a definition with the noun of its type.
  - [`@spec a-definition-is-said-in-markdown-the-way-a-formula-is`](#spec-a-definition-is-said-in-markdown-the-way-a-formula-is) — In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer says a definition with a blank line between its paragraphs.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-a-noun-phrase-for-each-kind) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - the alternatives of a [definition](#term-definition-passage) each begin with the kind of the subject
    > - the definition can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind)
    >
    > then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as a list with a noun phrase for each kind, such as "a spec that cites no axiom".
  - [`@spec the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or`](#spec-the-alternatives-of-one-kind-are-put-together-with-or) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has two alternatives for one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as one noun phrase for that kind, with the alternatives joined by or.
  - [`@spec the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination`](#spec-the-options-of-an-or-inside-a-kind-are-one-coordination) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has an or inside one kind and can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as one run of clauses joined by commas and or.
  - [`@spec a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence`](#spec-a-definition-with-one-kind-is-one-sentence) — When the alternatives of a [definition](#term-definition-passage) are of one kind and the definition can be said [kind by kind](#term-by-kind), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as one sentence.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-does-not-begin-with-its-kind`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-does-not-begin-with-its-kind) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has an alternative that does not begin with its kind, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-a-run-of-and-would-read-two-ways`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-a-run-of-and-would-read-two-ways) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has a run of "and" beside another alternative of its kind, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-is-not-about-its-subject`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-an-alternative-is-not-about-its-subject) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has an alternative that says something about another unit, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-two-of-its-kinds-can-share-a-member`](#spec-a-definition-by-cases-is-said-as-it-stands-when-two-of-its-kinds-can-share-a-member) — When a [definition](#term-definition-passage) has two kinds that can share a member, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the definition as a list of the alternatives as they stand.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-names-a-term-links-to-the-unit-that-holds-its-reading-in-markdown`](#spec-a-word-that-names-a-term-links-to-the-unit-that-holds-its-reading-in-markdown) — In the Markdown layout, the verbalizer links a word whose reading a unit holds to that unit.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-names-a-term-is-plain-in-the-text-layout`](#spec-a-word-that-names-a-term-is-plain-in-the-text-layout) — In the text layout, the verbalizer says a word whose reading a unit holds in plain words.
  - [`@spec only-the-first-mention-of-a-term-links`](#spec-only-the-first-mention-of-a-term-links) — In a [linked formula](#term-linked-formula), the verbalizer links only the first mention of a term, in reading order.
  - [`@spec a-word-never-links-to-the-unit-its-sentence-is-in`](#spec-a-word-never-links-to-the-unit-its-sentence-is-in) — The verbalizer never links a word to the unit whose statement it is saying.
  - [`@spec a-reading-that-points-at-a-unit-links-to-it`](#spec-a-reading-that-points-at-a-unit-links-to-it) — The verbalizer links a word whose reading points at a unit to that unit.
  - [`@spec a-link-in-a-table-held-in-another-document-goes-through-its-path`](#spec-a-link-in-a-table-held-in-another-document-goes-through-its-path) — The verbalizer writes a link of a table held in another document, to an anchor of that document, through the path to it.
  - [`@spec the-nouns-of-a-quantifier-link-and-the-article-follows-the-word`](#spec-the-nouns-of-a-quantifier-link-and-the-article-follows-the-word) — The verbalizer links the noun of a quantified type whose reading a unit holds, and chooses the article by the word, not the bracket.
  - [`@spec a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-on-the-word-and-not-on-the-bracket`](#spec-a-sentence-starts-with-a-capital-on-the-word-and-not-on-the-bracket) — When a statement begins with a linked word, the verbalizer puts the capital on the first letter of the word, inside the link.
  - [`@spec a-reading-held-by-no-unit-has-plain-words`](#spec-a-reading-held-by-no-unit-has-plain-words) — The verbalizer says a word whose reading no unit holds in plain words, even in the Markdown layout.
  - [`@spec a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase`](#spec-a-variable-said-once-takes-the-place-of-its-quantifier-as-a-noun-phrase) — When the sentence says the variable of a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) once and the quantifier [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier as a noun phrase in the place of the variable, such as "sits in no unit".
  - [`@spec a-noun-phrase-can-be-the-subject-of-a-sentence`](#spec-a-noun-phrase-can-be-the-subject-of-a-sentence) — When the variable of a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) is the subject of the sentence and the quantifier [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier with the noun phrase as the subject, such as "a tag names unit_1".
  - [`@spec what-else-is-true-of-the-variable-is-a-relative-clause`](#spec-what-else-is-true-of-the-variable-is-a-relative-clause) — When the variable of a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) has a further condition and the quantifier [fits](#term-fit) a noun phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier with a relative clause, such as "a unit that is a spec".
  - [`@spec several-negations-of-a-variable-are-one-negation`](#spec-several-negations-of-a-variable-are-one-negation) — The verbalizer says several negations of a variable as one negation that lists the kinds, when the quantifier fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another`](#spec-a-variable-that-must-differ-from-another-of-its-kind-is-said-as-another) — The verbalizer says a variable that must differ from another of its kind as "another" before the noun, when the [quantifier](#term-quantifier) fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec a-variable-that-must-differ-from-one-value-is-said-as-other-than-it`](#spec-a-variable-that-must-differ-from-one-value-is-said-as-other-than-it) — When the [quantifier](#term-quantifier) fits a noun phrase, the verbalizer says a variable that must differ from one value as its noun "other than" the value. The value is a variable or a string, as in "a text other than "a"". It says a variable that must differ from several values in full.
  - [`@spec variables-of-different-kinds-nest-as-phrases`](#spec-variables-of-different-kinds-nest-as-phrases) — The verbalizer says variables of different kinds as nested phrases, when the quantifier fits a noun phrase.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-whose-variable-would-be-said-twice-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-quantifier-whose-variable-would-be-said-twice-is-said-in-full) — When the reading of a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) says the variable twice, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-with-nothing-to-attach-to-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-quantifier-with-nothing-to-attach-to-is-said-in-full) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) has no fact for its variable beside another thing
    > - at least one of these holds:
    >   - the variable of the quantifier is not the subject of the sentence
    >   - the quantifier has more than three conditions, or conditions longer than a line and is under "no"
    >   - the quantifier is under "no" with a condition that says "no"
    >
    > then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-about-its-variable-alone-is-said-with-there-is-and-that`](#spec-a-quantifier-about-its-variable-alone-is-said-with-there-is-and-that) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) has no fact for its variable beside another thing
    > - the variable of the quantifier is the subject of the sentence
    > - the quantifier has three conditions or fewer that fit a line
    > - the quantifier is not under "no" with a condition that says "no"
    > - the quantifier does not both say that no variable differs from another and hold a condition
    >
    > then the following holds:
    >
    > [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier as "there is" with its noun and a relative clause, such as "there is a unit that is a spec", or under "no" with one condition, such as "no unit is a spec".
  - [`@spec many-conditions-about-a-variable-alone-are-bullets-after-there-is-that`](#spec-many-conditions-about-a-variable-alone-are-bullets-after-there-is-that) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) has no fact for its variable beside another thing
    > - the variable of the quantifier is the subject of the sentence
    > - the quantifier has more than three conditions, or conditions longer than a line
    > - the quantifier is not under "no"
    > - the quantifier does not both say that no variable differs from another and hold a condition
    >
    > then the following holds:
    >
    > [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier as "there is" with its noun and "that", and its conditions as bullets below it without their subject.
  - [`@spec no-with-another-is-said-in-full`](#spec-no-with-another-is-said-in-full) — When a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) says no variable differs from another and holds a condition, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-quantifier-with-a-time-phrase-in-one-of-several-conditions-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-quantifier-with-a-time-phrase-in-one-of-several-conditions-is-said-in-full) — When the following holds: a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) has several conditions, one of which begins with a time phrase then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec a-condition-that-is-not-about-the-variable-is-said-in-full`](#spec-a-condition-that-is-not-about-the-variable-is-said-in-full) — When the condition of a [quantifier](#term-quantifier) is not about its variable, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the quantifier in full, with "there is" and the numbered name.
  - [`@spec three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence`](#spec-three-clauses-or-fewer-are-said-in-a-sentence) — When a [list](#term-series) can be put in a [sentence](#term-sentenceable), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list in a sentence.
  - [`@spec a-longer-list-or-a-list-with-a-comma-is-bullets`](#spec-a-longer-list-or-a-list-with-a-comma-is-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) is a run of clauses joined by and or by or and cannot be put in a [sentence](#term-sentenceable), [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-of-more-than-three-clauses-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-of-more-than-three-clauses-is-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) has more than three clauses, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-with-a-comma-in-an-item-and-more-than-two-clauses-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-with-a-comma-in-an-item-and-more-than-two-clauses-is-bullets) —
      > When all of these hold:
      > - a [list](#term-series) has an item that holds a comma
      > - the list has more than two clauses
      >
      > then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-too-long-for-a-line-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-too-long-for-a-line-is-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) is longer than a line when it is put in a sentence, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-with-a-time-phrase-before-its-last-clause-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-with-a-time-phrase-before-its-last-clause-is-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) has a clause before its last that begins with a time phrase, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-with-a-relative-clause-before-its-last-clause-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-with-a-relative-clause-before-its-last-clause-is-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) has a clause before its last with a relative clause in it, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
    - [`@spec a-list-with-a-clause-that-holds-its-own-and-or-or-is-bullets`](#spec-a-list-with-a-clause-that-holds-its-own-and-or-or-is-bullets) — The verbalizer says a list as bullets when a clause in it has two names for a subject: "o and p are the same".
    - [`@spec an-item-that-is-more-than-a-clause-makes-the-list-bullets`](#spec-an-item-that-is-more-than-a-clause-makes-the-list-bullets) — When a [list](#term-series) has an item that is more than one clause, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets.
  - [`@spec negative-clauses-that-share-their-words-are-said-once-before-none-of-these`](#spec-negative-clauses-that-share-their-words-are-said-once-before-none-of-these) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [list](#term-series) is a run of negative clauses about one subject that share their verb, each before a noun phrase of its own
    > - [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list as bullets
    >
    > then verbalizer says the subject and the verb that the clauses of the list share once, before "none of these".
  - [`@spec an-and-inside-an-or-is-kept-apart`](#spec-an-and-inside-an-or-is-kept-apart) — For every [list_1](#term-series): when list_1 is a list of alternatives where one alternative holds an and, [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says list_1 as bullets that cannot be read two ways.
  - [`@spec words-said-once-for-several-clauses-hold-no-noun-phrase`](#spec-words-said-once-for-several-clauses-hold-no-noun-phrase) — Where the verbalizer says once the words that several clauses share, those words hold no noun phrase. They are the subject, and at most the verb after it.
  - [`@spec a-subject-is-said-once-when-clauses-begin-with-it`](#spec-a-subject-is-said-once-when-clauses-begin-with-it) — In a list said as a sentence, the verbalizer says once a subject that its clauses begin with.
  - [`@spec a-pair-of-variables-is-said-as-it-is-and-not-as-a-subject`](#spec-a-pair-of-variables-is-said-as-it-is-and-not-as-a-subject) — In a list said as a sentence, the verbalizer says a clause about a pair of variables as it is, not as a shared subject.
  - [`@spec a-rule-keeps-its-then-before-a-time-phrase`](#spec-a-rule-keeps-its-then-before-a-time-phrase) —
    > When all of these hold:
    > - a [list](#term-series) is a rule whose two sides are each one clause
    > - the list is not a rule whose first side begins with a time phrase
    > - the list is a rule whose second side begins with a time phrase
    >
    > then [verbalizer](#term-verbalizer) says the list with "then" before the time phrase.
  - [`@spec a-rule-drops-its-then-before-anything-else`](#spec-a-rule-drops-its-then-before-anything-else) —
    > When all of these hold:
